nodes.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a preordered set $Y$. If $f$ has a strict local maximum at $a \in X$, then $f$ has a local maximum at $a$, that is, $f(x) \le f(a)$ for all $x$ in some neighborhood of $a$.
nodes.title: A strict local maximum is a local maximum

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a preordered set $Y$. If $f$ has a strict local minimum at $a \in X$, then $f$ has a local minimum at $a$, that is, $f(a) \le f(x)$ for all $x$ in some neighborhood of $a$.
nodes.title: A strict local minimum is a local minimum

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f''(x_0) < 0$, $f'(x_0) = 0$, and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, then $f$ has a strict local maximum at $x_0$.
nodes.title: Strict second-derivative test, maximum version

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a set $Y$ equipped with a relation $<$. Then $f$ has a strict local maximum at a point $a \in X$ if $f(x) < f(a)$ for all $x \ne a$ in some neighborhood of $a$.
nodes.title: Strict local maximum

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f''(x_0) > 0$, $f'(x_0) = 0$, and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, then $f$ has a strict local minimum at $x_0$.
nodes.title: Strict second-derivative test, minimum version

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a set $Y$ equipped with a relation $<$. Then $f$ has a strict local minimum at a point $a \in X$ if $f(a) < f(x)$ for all $x \ne a$ in some neighborhood of $a$.
nodes.title: Strict local minimum

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $Y$ be an additive group with a relation $<$ such that addition on the left and addition on the right are strictly monotone. If $f \colon X \to Y$ has a strict local maximum at $a \in X$, then $x \mapsto -f(x)$ has a strict local minimum at $a$.
nodes.title: Negation turns a strict local maximum into a strict local minimum

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $Y$ be an additive group with a relation $<$ such that addition on the left and addition on the right are strictly monotone. If $f \colon X \to Y$ has a strict local minimum at $a \in X$, then $x \mapsto -f(x)$ has a strict local maximum at $a$.
nodes.title: Negation turns a strict local minimum into a strict local maximum

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
